records.title: Euler V1 donateToReserves solvency-check exploit
records.rootCauseSummary: Euler V1's donateToReserves path could reduce an account's collateral position without the account-health check required to prevent the user from intentionally entering an unhealthy state. The attacker combined that solvency-check omission with Euler's liquidation mechanics to create an attacker-controlled liquidatable position and capture a liquidation bonus greater than the economic loss caused by the donation.
records.attackSummary: The attacker used flash liquidity and Euler's leverage/accounting paths, donated collateral through donateToReserves to become liquidatable without a post-donation solvency rejection, then used a second attacker-controlled account to self-liquidate the unhealthy position and extract value from Euler liquidity. The incident was executed across multiple transactions and assets; the first DAI exploit transaction is preserved as the representative onchain anchor for this record.
preconditions: A funded Euler V1 market with withdrawable underlying liquidity.
The deployed donateToReserves behavior lacks the required post-action account health check.
An attacker can establish a leveraged collateral/debt position and control both the violator and liquidator roles.
Liquidation incentives can compensate the attacker-controlled liquidator for liquidating the deliberately unhealthy position.
Sufficient temporary liquidity is available to establish the attack position.
attackSteps: Acquire temporary liquidity and establish a leveraged Euler V1 position.
Use donateToReserves to reduce the violator account's collateral without a post-donation health check rejecting the resulting unhealthy state.
Use a second attacker-controlled account to liquidate the deliberately unhealthy violator position.
Capture liquidation value greater than the attacker's donation loss and withdraw real underlying liquidity.
Repeat the exploit shape across additional Euler markets/assets during the broader incident.
violatedProperties: Any user action that materially reduces collateral backing debt must preserve account solvency or revert before committing the unhealthy state.
A user must not be able to manufacture a profitable liquidation of an attacker-controlled account solely by using protocol accounting operations.
Liquidation incentives and reserve accounting must not allow attacker-created accounting state to redeem against unrelated depositor liquidity without equivalent economic backing.
applicabilitySignals: A user-callable donation or reserve-transfer path can reduce collateral bookkeeping while debt remains outstanding.
The donation/reserve path does not perform the same solvency or liquidity check enforced after ordinary collateral-reducing operations.
Liquidation can be initiated by an independently controlled account against the deliberately unhealthy position.
Liquidation reward/yield is redeemable for real underlying protocol liquidity.
Leverage or temporary liquidity can amplify the size of the deliberately unhealthy position.
nonApplicabilitySignals: Every collateral-reducing donation/reserve path enforces an account health check before state is committed.
Donated balances cannot reduce collateral that backs outstanding debt.
The protocol has no liquidation path or liquidation cannot transfer economically valuable collateral/yield to an attacker-controlled counterparty.
The tested deployment does not contain the vulnerable Euler V1 donateToReserves semantics.
falsePositiveGuards: Confirm the exact target path can make a debt-bearing account less healthy; a cosmetic reserve donation is not sufficient.
Confirm the target lacks an equivalent post-action solvency check on the relevant deployed path rather than inferring vulnerability from function naming.
Confirm an attacker-controlled liquidation can produce net extractable value after the donation loss and transaction/flash-liquidity costs.
Do not transfer Euler V1-specific conclusions to Euler V2 or unrelated modular lending deployments without independent source/runtime matching.
runtimeRequirements: Historical reproduction must bind the Euler V1 deployed code/state at the selected pre-exploit block rather than current Euler V2 state.
limitations: This record uses the first representative DAI exploit transaction as its exact transaction/block anchor; that transaction is not the entire approximately $197M incident.
Euler's official account documents multiple exploit transactions across additional assets after the representative DAI exploit transaction.
The overall USD loss estimate is approximate and applies to the multi-transaction incident, not solely to the representative DAI transaction.
No HISTORICAL_REPRODUCTION or GENERALIZED_VARIANT_PROVEN claim is made at K07; those proof obligations remain for later modules.
